**Sept 2024 study (FY22–FY24):** [AIR News](https://www.newsonair.gov.in/sebi-study-reveals-individual-traders-face-severe-losses-in-equity-fo-segment); [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/capital-market-news/sebi-study-exposes-massive-losses-for-individual-f-o-traders-in-india-124092400948_1.html)
- About 93% of individuals lost money, with only 7.2% profitable over the three years.
- Aggregate losses exceeded ₹1.8 lakh crore, with an average of about ₹2 lakh per loss-maker.
- Only about 1% earned more than ₹1 lakh after costs.
- In FY24, prop traders made ₹33,000 crore and FPIs ₹28,000 crore in gross trading profits, "mostly by entities using algorithms".

**Aug 2026 study, "Profitability of Individual Traders in the Equity Derivatives Segment (FY25–FY26)"** (Patankar and Rath, SEBI DEPA-II): [SEBI PDF](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/aug-2026/1787233506209.pdf)
- **Losses and participants:**
  - Aggregate individual net losses were ₹91,685 crore in FY26, down 18% from a revised ₹1.12 lakh crore in FY25.
  - 87.7% of individuals were loss-makers in FY26, against 90.9% in FY25.
  - The average loss per person rose 2%.
  - Active individuals fell 18–20%, from 98.1 lakh to 78.6 lakh in the sample, and new entrants fell about 40% to 20.8 lakh.
- **Options are where the losses are:**
  - Options were 92% of individual losses.
  - Loss incidence was 87.7% in options against 66.0% in futures.
  - 99.3% of individuals traded options at least once, and 93% traded only options.
- **Gross P&L by category (Chart 19 / Table 11), FY25 → FY26:**

  | Category | FY25 (₹ crore) | FY26 (₹ crore) |
  |---|---|---|
  | Prop traders | 45,955 | 44,483 |
  | FPIs | 31,085 | 13,896 |
  | Corporates | 8,092 (chart) / 8,280 (table) | 5,960 |
  | Mutual funds | 5,613 | 2,595 |
  | Partnership firms / LLPs | 4,737 | 2,953 |
  | Individuals | −97,882 | −72,243 |

`case_study:tesla-2010-2024` · tickers US-TSLA · confidence: verified

Split-adjusted (5:1 2020, 3:1 2022 = 15x): IPO June 2010 $17 (~$1.13). June 2019 low just under $177 (~$11.8) amid Model 3 cash fears. Peak Nov 2021 ~$414 (closing ~$410): ~35x in 2.5 years. Then -73% to ~$101 (Jan 2023) on demand worries, price cuts and Musk's Twitter purchase/share sales; -65% in calendar 2022 alone. New high ~$488 (Dec 2024) on robotaxi/policy hopes [unverified]. Split: overwhelmingly rerating — GAAP profits only began 2020; at the 2021 peak the market cap exceeded most automakers combined while P/E was >100x. EPS did grow fast 2020-22, then fell 2023-24 as auto margins collapsed from ~30% to <20% [unverified]. EARLY SIGNAL visible mid/late 2019: Model 3 run-rate ~5k/week sustained, a surprise Q3 2019 profit, Shanghai Gigafactory built in ~10 months — i.e., the existential risk was ending while short interest was extreme. Who caught it: Baron Funds (Ron Baron, long-time holder from ~2014, publicly), ARK Invest (Cathie Wood's 2018 $4,000 pre-split target), Baillie Gifford (early holder, trimmed 2020-22) [holder details from memory, unverified]. Stall: 2024 was the first annual delivery decline; valuation now rests on autonomy/robotics optionality. LESSON: when survival risk resolves in a heavily shorted category-creator, the rerating can be violent; but a price driven mostly by multiple is fragile and swings -60-75% repeatedly.

- **Start → end:** ~$11.8 split-adj (Jun 2019); IPO $1.13 adj → ~$414 (Nov 2021); ~$488 (Dec 2024) [unverified] (~35x (2019-21); ~400x from IPO)
- **EPS vs rerating:** mostly rerating
- **Max drawdown:** -73% (Nov 2021-Jan 2023)
- **Early signal:** Model 3 ramp, Q3 2019 profit, Shanghai plant speed, extreme short interest
- **Who caught it:** Ron Baron, Cathie Wood/ARK, Baillie Gifford [unverified details]
- **Ended/stalled:** deliveries fell 2024; narrative-driven since
- **Lesson:** survival-risk resolution rerates; multiple-driven prices are fragile
- **Sources:** [1](https://www.cnbc.com/2019/12/23/tesla-stock-reaches-420-per-share.html) · [2](https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/03/30/tesla-stock-dropped-50-high-this-will-happen-next/) · [3](https://insideevs.com/news/628181/tesla-stock-has-worst-year-to-date-is-down-almost-70-percent-ytd/) · [4](https://www.opb.org/article/2023/01/06/tesla-s-stock-lost-over-700-billion-in-value-elon-musk-s-twitter-deal-didn-t-help/)
